title: Nothing Is Everlasting
subtitle: No eternity on earth, only a fleeting moment.

items.text:
Is it real, our elusive existence?
               No eternity on earth, only a fleeting moment.
               Be it as resilient as jade, it shatters;
               Be it as revered as gold, it crumbles;
               Be it as resplendent as quetzal plumes, it will fall away.
               No eternity on earth, only a fleeting moment.

                                             —Cantares mexicanos
Guided by instinct, she moves forward, step by step.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Finally, above this endless churning water, she sees a figure standing still as a statue, pallid as a ghost.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: It's been a long time, Teresita.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: María, Antonio, Carmen, and I ... We've all missed you very much.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Welcome back.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Muriel! Ah, when did you return from Europe?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: How many years have passed since then? I can't seem to remember at all.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Well, please, tell me all about your time in Paris.
He wears a strange, sorrowful expression.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Where do I begin? A lot has happened over the past four years.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I encountered an arcanist organization called Manus Vindictae. With their help, I survived an event called the "Storm." Many times, in fact. But by the time I returned home, I realized everyone I knew had perished.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: What I returned to was no longer the Mexico I knew.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Oh, my dear Muriel. I'm so sorry to hear it.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Perhaps María and I shouldn't have sent you to Europe.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: But I learned so much there.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: While I was in Paris, I learned from Professor Roseau's research. His efforts to find a resurrection ritual led us to discover Depths of Myth, the sea of humanity's collective unconscious.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: His failure proved that a successful resurrection requires the alignment of multiple nearly impossible conditions, but at least the professor's research pointed me in the right direction.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Do you recall the Temazcal ceremony we once talked about?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: The cleansing ritual?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: That's the one. Drawing from the Temazcal ceremony, Professor Roseau's research, and countless other texts, I have finally created the ultimate ritual of resurrection.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Using special herbs and arcane skills as a catalyst, we may transfer our existence into a painting, where we'll be enveloped by absolute darkness.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: And within that primal void, we can regain our purest consciousness and rediscover who we truly are, who we were meant to be.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The ritual requires a unique arcane silver ore, which I was fortunate to find here in this era's Vale of Tears.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: From it, I crafted a pigment of infinite malleability, one capable of recreating almost anything, even our memories and identities.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The sea of collective unconscious is the deepest layer of the human mind, the origin of all things.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Rest assured, Teresita. I will reconstruct you completely, body and mind, from the Depths of Myth.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: I'm not sure I entirely follow. But I see that you are every bit the genius I always knew you were, Muriel.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Who else would connect resurrection rituals to an ancient sweat lodge ceremony?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I've tried everything over the years, but I finally found a method that works, Teresita.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I'm so thankful that I've found you again.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: I'm happy you have, too, from the bottom of my heart. But I almost feel as if I've forgotten something important.
The roiling water slows into soft and silent ripples.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Now is the year of 1920, the start of a decade you and María once longed for.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The muralist movement has just begun. I'll ensure we won't make the same mistakes we did last time.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Haha, it isn't like you to care about anything beyond your paintings.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: People change.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: It was only after I left you and the others that I realized how lucky I was to live a life completely dedicated to my art.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: But we have changed for the better, Muriel. You've grown up. Can take care of yourself now. You no longer need María or me to protect you.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: Knowing that, I can continue my search for what I've forgotten.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Is it really so important? More important than our dream? Than María, Antonio, all our friends of the Midnight Kitchen?

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: It is. It's only a haze to me, but deep down I know it is more important than anything.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: I'm sorry, Muriel. Until I find it, I can't pursue our dream with you.
Though confused, she keeps walking forward.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You mustn't go any farther, Teresita.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The deeper you go, the weaker my ritual becomes. Your mind's essence might be completely erased from the Depths of Myth.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Are you truly certain you want to leave, knowing your very existence could be wiped out?
She doesn't stop.
False memories in vivid color begin to peel from her skin like new paint stripped from a canvas.
Their joy, their dreams, the time they shared—layer by layer, they fall into the water below.

items.speaker: Teresita
items.text: It's so beautiful.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Those memories, they shine, glitter like crystal.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Thank you for showing them to me, Muriel.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But you have to understand: nothing lasts forever. Death is part of the cycle of life, just like any other stage.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The future you dream about warmed my heart, it did, but it doesn't belong to me.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Just like those memories you forced into my mind.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Now, I need to find my true self. I need to find Ramona.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Please stop, Teresita.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Please don't do this to me. I can't lose you again.
His dim figure begins to glow.
Memories cling to him like shards of sharpened glass until he takes on the form of a shining broken god.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: The spirits followed the marigolds all the way from the mansion in Roma to the People's Library, a final touch to complete the mural. Quite a night.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I've got you now.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Ah!
Muriel looks up toward the finished mural.
The paint has cracked alongside the plaster. At last, the trapped form inside returns to the world.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Teresita, it's you.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The ritual worked! Professor Roseau was right.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: What are we to do next, Teresita?
His eyes shine with the joy of a dream so long awaited, finally realized in the flesh.
Standing there in front of him, Ramona takes a deep and weighty breath.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: It's over, Muriel.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You're the serial killer. It was all you.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You used a special pigment to make paintings with arcane powers—your murder weapons—and passed them out to the victims through the club.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: And then, you activated a ritual through the painting to kill your target.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You killed all seven of them, all to get the friends you lost to the "Storm" back.
She glances back to the cracked and battered mural behind her.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Those people in the mural ... Your friends from the Midnight Kitchen, aren't they?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: María, Carmen, Antonio, Laura ...
She names each face that appeared in the shattered memories. Her eyes rest on the very center.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: And Teresita.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Who'd have ever thought those faces would match the victims almost perfectly?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: To think how often I walked through this hall and never made the connection.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: They were my best friends.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: My countrymen. My comrades.
He lifts the flowerpot in his hands, eager.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Before I left Mexico, you gave me some dahlia seeds. Do you remember that?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You said we'd meet again when the dahlias were in full bloom.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: So I carry the pot wherever I go. I care for them no matter the circumstances.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I'm so glad we finally met again, just as you promised.
Ramona struggles to find a response. She studies his face, hoping to find something in it that might help her decide between pity and horror.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: In all seven murders, you didn't manage to pull off a single one of your resurrection rituals, did you?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I don't understand what you're saying.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I saw you in the painting, Muriel, in that void.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: A little younger, a hell of a lot saner than you are now, but you all the same.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I'd been thinking, the fragmented memories I saw in the Depths of Myth, where are they from? Who do they belong to?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But seeing you now, I think I get it.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You didn't reconstruct Teresita's consciousness from the Depths of Myth, not one bit.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Those memories and feelings were painted into the mural by you. They all came from you, Muriel.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That's why I could only see memories of you and Teresita together.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: All the moments you shared with your friends, the memories you held so close that you couldn't just let the dead be dead. You've given them up, sealed their spirits inside your paintings.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You completed the rituals, but you destroyed yourself.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: When? H-How did I?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: No, Teresita, I-I didn't.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: See? I'm not Teresita, and you still can't see it.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Your dearest friend and mentor ... And yet you still mistake me for her, a complete stranger.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The moment you finished this mural, you scrubbed every last trace of her clean from your mind. You aren't even yourself anymore.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: All those people killed, and for what? The delusions of a man in the middle of destroying himself?
Muriel speaks to himself, clutching his head as if in pain.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: You mean there's no way to save my friends? I killed them with my own hands.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I ... No, Teresita.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Why can't I remember your face? Your voice?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: The memories ... Why won't they come to me? My most cherished friends, my family ...

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: No. If I forget, then they will truly be gone. What must I do?

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Wait. You said my memories are sealed within these paintings. Is that true?
He raises his paintbrush, lost in abject sorrow, yet sparkling with sudden determination.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: What are you doing, Muriel? Stop!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The Vigiles will get here any minute. You don't stand a—

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I remember it now. You're Ms. Ramona. You work with the Vigiles Bureau.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: I apologize for all the trouble I've caused. It seems I've made one mistake after another.
For the last time, he uses his arcane skill.
Perfect strokes of colorful paint wrap around him like a consuming fire.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: And it's too late to right all my wrongs. Thank you for putting an end to this tragedy of mine.

items.speaker: Muriel
items.text: Now the only thing left to do is to cross the tides of time and return to their warm embrace.
A rare smile touches his lips, as if he were drifting into a warm and pleasant dream as he fades away.
Light, shadow, and color coalesce around him, shrinking as he disappears until all that's left is a single painted hummingbird. It flies up toward the mural and joins the circle.
His brush clatters on the solid floor.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: All these deaths ... If only I'd realized the truth sooner ...

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I'm sorry, Muriel. You tried so hard, but I'm not Teresita. I could never be.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: There are still so many things only Ramona can do.
A long silence follows. It takes Ramona a moment to regain her composure, and she becomes that jaded exorcist she tries so hard to be.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Looks like I gotta report this now. Case is closed.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Tch, can't a girl get one peaceful night?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Never should've taken this damned job.
She gathers her feelings and leaves the building without another thought.
Some time after Ramona departs, another figure emerges from the darkness.
He raises a hand toward the bullet hole in the mural, as if soothing a scar that will never heal.
Quite the tragedy.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I was wondering which corner you might be watching from. So you came, after all, Ms. Butterfly.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I couldn't miss the grand finale.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Tell me, are you satisfied? You are the one who orchestrated it all.
